title: BDD test suite
description: Generated by Build-Schema.ps1 from suite.core.json, actions.catalog.yaml and what it imports. Do not edit: regenerate it, and run the generator with -Check in CI so a stale copy fails the build.

suite.description: The suite name. Unique per file, and the name the report groups cases under.

imports.description: Declaration libraries this suite pulls in, resolved depth-first in listed order, relative to this file. A library declares params, vars, metaSteps and defaults, and nothing that runs.

beforeEachTimeoutSec.description: Bounds the beforeEach block, once per case.

afterEachTimeoutSec.description: Bounds the afterEach block, once per case.

setup.description: Runs once, before the first selected case, into a suite capture bag every case starts from a copy of.

afterEach.description: Runs after every selected case, whether it passed.

teardown.description: Runs once, after the last case, whether cases passed. Its failure is its own entry in the report.

tests.description: The cases. A case is what passes or fails, and its name is what appears in the report.

owner.description: The team that maintains this suite.

limit.description: A time limit in whole seconds, or an expression that yields one. The ceiling it is checked against is in diagnostics.md; a runtime extension may add a stricter one.

defaults.description: Values every case in the file inherits, and may override.

timeoutSec.description: The deadline every case inherits, covering its steps and assertions.

cleanupTimeoutSec.description: The window a case cleanup gets, even after the case timed out.

vars.description: Values calculated inside the file, in declaration order, each an expression.

expression.description: A value, or a string containing one or more ${ } expressions.

paramDeclList.description: Parameters this file declares. A case restates one under its own params to override it for that case.

input.description: Supplied by whoever starts the run (--param, or the runtime's parameter environment variable, BDD_SUITE_PARAM_<NAME> by default), so it has no default on purpose. E210 accepts it without one.

metaStep.description: A named, ordered list of steps, declared once and used by name with - meta: <name>.

override.description: Declares that this definition replaces one of the same name from an imported library. Without it the collision is E209.

exports.description: The capture names this definition publishes to the case that used it.

examples.description: Runs this case once per row, reporting once per row as <name> [<column>=<value>, ...], with ${row.<column>} bound for the whole case. Two identical rows are E213, because two report entries cannot share a name.

assert.description: One subject and one or more comparisons, all of which must pass. A subject with no comparison is E204, which is what catches a misspelled operator.

var.description: A dotted path into the capture bag of the case.

equals.description: The subject as a string equals this, ignoring case.

notEquals.description: The subject as a string differs from this, ignoring case.

contains.description: A list subject has this as a member; any other subject has it as a substring, ignoring case.

notContains.description: The negation of contains, with the same coercion.

startsWith.description: The subject as a string begins with this, ignoring case.

endsWith.description: The subject as a string ends with this, ignoring case.

matches.description: The subject as a string matches this regular expression, ignoring case. Restricted to the subset RE2 and .NET agree on: a backreference, a lookahead or a lookbehind is E308.

in.description: The subject is a member of this list.

gt.description: Both sides as 64-bit floats, subject greater. A non-numeric operand fails the assertion with a type message, never silently as false.

gte.description: Both sides as 64-bit floats, subject greater or equal. A non-numeric operand fails with a type message.

lt.description: Both sides as 64-bit floats, subject smaller. A non-numeric operand fails with a type message.

lte.description: Both sides as 64-bit floats, subject smaller or equal. A non-numeric operand fails with a type message.

count.description: The subject is a list whose length equals this.

isTrue.description: The subject is the boolean true, not a truthy string.

isFalse.description: The subject is the boolean false, not a falsy string.

isNull.description: The path is absent or null.

isNotNull.description: The path is present and not null.

script.description: A PowerShell expression that must return truthy. Implemented by the PowerShell binding only.

sentence.description: What this step means, in the language of the thing being tested rather than the language of the action. It is what the report and every failure print.

why.description: Why this step exists, in the reader's words: one line, shown beside the step's sentence in reports and tools.

table.description: Named columns and rows. A step that carries one runs once per row, in row order, with ${row.<column>} bound; a case that carries one under examples runs once per row and reports once per row. Every row declares the same columns, and no two rows are identical. A table with no rows is E213 rather than a structural error, so the message can say that the step it drives would never run.

stepCommon.$comment: Not a schema any document is validated against. The generator copies these properties into every per-action branch, so a field every step carries is written down once.

given.description: The state this step establishes. One Gherkin keyword per step, and the order within a list is given, then when, then then.

then.description: The outcome this step observes. Its expectation belongs in its own asserts.

and.description: Continues the keyword of the step before it. First in a list it is E212, because there is nothing to continue.

timeoutSec.description: This step's own limit. The effective limit is the smaller of it and what remains of the case deadline: a step may shorten its share and may never lengthen it. An action that takes an internal bound, such as a poll or a drain wait, reads this same number.

captureAs.description: Publishes the return value of this step under this name, read as ${capture.<name>}. With a table, it publishes a list with one entry per row, in row order.

ifCapture.description: Runs the step only when this capture name or dotted object-field path is present. Null and false are present; an absent field skips the step.

table.description: Runs this step once per row, with ${row.<column>} bound to that row.

asserts.description: Checked immediately after this step and before the next one, inside this step's own limit. The case-level asserts block still runs after every step.

stepEnvelope.$comment: What every step has in common, with no per-action checking. A validator whose JSON Schema implementation reports errors from unselected conditional branches validates the document against this and each step against its own generated branch; that produces the same diagnostics without the noise.

step.meta.description: A meta step use site. It publishes the exports of the definition by name and so carries no captureAs.
